public_rationale: The Register reported on April 16, 2026 that Anthropic began moving enterprise customers to usage-based billing at renewal in November 2025 and introduced a revised plan in February 2026. This establishes billing changes, but not withdrawal of a subsidy measured against actual costs [e1]. On May 6, Anthropic announced increased Claude Code limits for several subscription plans [e2]. Neither item establishes deliberate concealment or material customer or commercial deterioration caused by subsidy withdrawal during January 1–June 15, 2026 [e1, e2].
limitations: Neither evidence item concerns OpenAI [e1, e2].
The evidence provides no matched provider-cost records or representative customer results establishing the causal chain [e1, e2].
Higher usage limits alone establish neither cost-covering service nor customer retention [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI labs intentionally obscured the costs of subscriptions and heavily subsidized users' compute, and now that this has changed, everything has begun to fall apart.

statement.excerpt: I’ve been saying for years that the underlying economics of AI don’t make sense — that AI labs were intentionally obfuscating the costs of subscriptions and heavily subsidizing users’ compute, and that the moment that that changed, everything would begin to fall apart, and god damn has it finally begun.

from_speaker: AI labs were intentionally obfuscating the costs of subscriptions
everything would begin to fall apart
our_interpretation: The context principally identifies OpenAI and Anthropic, rather than every AI provider.
The ordinary reading is that deliberate cost opacity and substantial below-cost usage supported demand, and withdrawing that support caused material customer or commercial deterioration.
The recent causal episode runs from the alleged early-Q1 billing changes through June 15. Earlier subsidy practices are background, not a separately dated financial observation.
Material deterioration means measurable cancellations, reduced usage, or worsening commercial results. Complaints alone are insufficient.
A discount from API list prices is not necessarily a subsidy relative to the provider's actual costs.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes deliberate concealment, substantial below-cost service, withdrawal of that support, and ensuing material deterioration attributable to the withdrawal rather than competing explanations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence shows a central asserted link is false, such as no actual subsidy withdrawal, no material deterioration among affected customers, or deterioration caused by another documented factor.

evidence.explanation: Usage allowances increased for several subscription plans during the alleged deterioration period. This complicates a uniform subsidy-withdrawal account, but does not establish actual costs or customer retention.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: For each company separately, dated billing and actual-cost records, direct evidence bearing on deliberate concealment, and affected-customer churn, usage and commercial results that distinguish subsidy withdrawal from capacity limits, product changes, competition and regulation.
